Theoretically I have nothing against this because the only reason we really bitch about ads at all is because of how intrusive they are and what a security risk they present.

However, this move should be coming from the websites themselves, not from a third party.

Except the websites themselves would never do this. There's a reason intrusive ads exist online. It's because I have no veto power when it comes to the poor decisions of a marketer deciding what to put on my screen.

It would be great if there were a built in option in each browser which you could choose "Non-intrusive ads only". But, 1) That would require the website to respect that option. 2) I doubt anyone who puts intrusive ads on their site has the integrity to respect an opt-out for intrusive ads.

So, we need a 3rd party to mediate. I'm willing to let Ad Block be this mediator. If they fuck up, some other Ad Block software will fill the void.

It's kind of like, back in the day, when browsers allowed pop-up windows. It was a feature which was seriously abused. We could have said "This change should be coming from the websites themselves". But it never did. It's still a huge problem. The only reason it's not a big deal anymore is because modern browsers said, "Hey, this feature was a bad idea." and turned the feature off.

Here's the lengths I have to go to, to have a sane browsing experience.

  • Turn off Javascript.

  • Install Ad Block.

  • Uninstall Flash.

I don't get many intrusive ads when I do this. But I know they still exist out there because when I use a browser without protection, I immediately am bombarded by intrusive media.

Website marketers will never stop using intrusive ads because there is no veto from the public.
